title: Trans*Power: Primary care for trans people in Lower Saxony: Using health care data, experiences with care, and participatory approaches to enhance medical care and medical education
summary:
Trans* individuals frequently encounter barriers in healthcare, including uncertainty among healthcare providers in addressing gender identity, insufficient knowledge among physicians, as well as experiences of stigma and discrimination. As a result, essential healthcare services are sometimes not accessed or are sought only at a delayed stage. At the same time, there is limited evidence on how trans* individuals in Germany perceive primary care and what their specific needs are. Similarly, little is known about the challenges faced by practice teams in general practice, gynaecological, and paediatric settings when caring for trans* patients, or about the extent to which gender-sensitive care is addressed in the education and training of medical and nursing professionals.

The Transpower project addresses these issues through a mixed-methods approach combining qualitative interviews, a large-scale survey, and the analysis of anonymised health insurance data. This includes interviews with trans individuals about their care experiences, interviews with members of their social environment, and interviews with primary care practice teams. In addition, nationwide online questionnaires are administered, and anonymised data from AOK Niedersachsen are analysed to examine treatment pathways, morbidity patterns, and the utilisation of healthcare services. Furthermore, curricula in medical and nursing education are systematically reviewed to identify existing gaps.

Based on these findings, recommendations will be developed in an expert workshop and through a Delphi survey to sustainably improve primary care for trans* individuals. The project follows a participatory approach and is continuously guided by an advisory board consisting of trans* persons.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
WP1 – Trans Persons (Qualitative Interviews and Survey)*
• Self-identification as a trans* person, including non-binary, genderqueer, or gender-nonconforming individuals.
• Age ≥ 14 years.
• Sufficient German language proficiency to participate in interviews conducted in spoken German (for WP1a).
• Sufficient ability to understand the study information and provide informed consent.

WP2 – Routinely Collected Health Insurance Data (AOK Niedersachsen)
• Inclusion of anonymized data sets of insured individuals for whom an ICD‑10 diagnosis F64.0 and/or a coded gender‑affirming surgery (OPS) has been recorded since 2022.
• No active recruitment of participants.

WP3 – Primary Care Practice Teams
• Employment as a physician or medical assistant in general practice, gynecology, or pediatrics.
• Age ≥ 18 years.
• Involvement in at least one consultation or treatment of a trans* person within the past 12 months.
• Sufficient German language proficiency to participate in interviews conducted in spoken German.
• Sufficient ability to understand the study information and provide informed consent.

WP4 – Individuals from the Social Environment of Trans Persons*
• Persons identified by trans* participants as part of their social environment (e.g., family members, friends, partners, supporters, accompanying persons).
• Age ≥ 14 years.
• Sufficient German language proficiency to participate in interviews conducted in spoken German.
• Sufficient ability to understand the study information and provide informed consent.

WP6 – Experts for Trans Health Care (Workshop and Delphi Survey)*
• Documented expertise in the healthcare of trans* persons (e.g., clinical, scientific, policy, or community-based expertise).
• Age ≥ 18 years.
• Sufficient German language proficiency to participate in the workshop and/or Delphi survey.
• Sufficient ability to understand the study information and provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
• Lack of adequate capacity to understand the study information and to provide informed consent to participate
• Insufficient proficiency in German to participate in interviews conducted in spoken German
